evidence: Cic. Sen. 44: quamquam immoderātīs epulīs caret senectūs, modicīs tamen convīviīs dēlectārī potest
terms.comment: Grants a fact; the main clause often has tamen. At the head of a sentence it also corrects what was just said: “and yet”.

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the subjunctive in classical prose; with an adjective or adverb, “however”
evidence: Ov. Met. 6.376: quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant
terms.comment: “As much as you like”: grants a supposition, or a fact put as one. With an adjective it needs no verb: quamvīs fertilis, however fertile.

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the indicative for a fact
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.53.1: ego etsī nihil habeō quod ad tē scrībam, scrībō tamen
terms.comment: Built on sī: “even if”, used of a fact. Often answered by tamen.

evidence: Ov. Pont. 1.3.39–40: cum bene sit clausae caveā Pandīone nātae, nītitur in silvās illa redīre suās
terms.comment: Concessive cum: the fact that might have stopped the main clause; often with tamen.

phrases.latin: quamquam immoderātīs epulīs caret senectūs, modicīs tamen convīviīs dēlectārī potest
phrases.english: although old age goes without lavish feasts, it can still enjoy modest dinners
though every parent’s own child is worthy of it

phrases.latin: quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant
phrases.english: though they are under water, under water they try to curse

phrases.latin: ego etsī nihil habeō quod ad tē scrībam, scrībō tamen quia tēcum loquī videor
phrases.english: though I have nothing to write to you, I write all the same, because I seem to be talking with you
You keep going on, though I understand.

phrases.latin: cum bene sit clausae caveā Pandīone nātae, nītitur in silvās illa redīre suās
phrases.english: though Pandion’s daughter is well off shut in her cage, she strains to go back to her woods
